purpose: Test whether the chain-compatible RDG selector also respects constitutive/Hodge structure and source-free Maxwell dynamics.

formulation.energy: H=1/2 E^T epsilon E + 1/2 B^T nu B
formulation.constraints: d0^T epsilon E and d2 B

uniformMedium.conclusion: With unit positive constitutive matrices, the chain-compatible translation selector commutes with the Maxwell generator; admitted and defect sectors evolve independently.

translationBreakingMedium.epsilon: diagonal edge mass: 1 on x=0 cells and 3 on x=1 cells
translationBreakingMedium.conclusion: The full Maxwell system remains energy- and constraint-compatible, but material contrast breaks selector invariance and transfers an initially admitted state into the defect sector.

interpretation.topologicalGate: [P,d]=0 is necessary but not sufficient for dynamical closure.
interpretation.constitutiveGate: The selected symmetry must also preserve epsilon and nu, equivalently the discrete Hodge/constitutive data.
interpretation.dynamicsGate: Only then does [P,K]=0 and the admitted sector become an invariant subsystem.
interpretation.experimentalMeaning: A detected Q-sector signal can be ordinary scattering from symmetry-breaking material structure; it is not by itself new physics.

verdict: The RDG selector closes source-free discrete Maxwell dynamics in a homogeneous symmetry-compatible medium. A standard positive inhomogeneous constitutive law reopens the channel and produces admitted-to-defect transfer without violating energy or Gauss constraints.
